Q: Can't execute jupyter notebook in terminal: "execution_count": null A:

As a workaround, I have created a script clean_notebook.py that removes the faulty lines:

# clean_notebook.py
import json
import pathlib
import sys
from copy import deepcopy

def clean_cell(cell):
    cell = deepcopy(cell)
    if cell.get("cell_type") == "code" and "execution_count" in cell:
        del cell["execution_count"]
    return cell

def main(nb_path):
    nb_path = pathlib.Path(nb_path)
    data = json.loads(nb_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    data["cells"] = [clean_cell(c) for c in data["cells"]]
    nb_path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"✔️ Cleaned {nb_path}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print("Usage: python clean_notebook.py <notebook.ipynb>")
        sys.exit(1)
    main(sys.argv[1])

run py clean_notebook.py Untitled.ipynb before your execution.

Q: dns propogation issue with cloudflare subdomain A:

This is a common DNS configuration issue. When your root subdomain (portfolios.shuttrbox.com) resolves but www.portfolios.shuttrbox.com doesn't, you're likely missing the specific CNAME record for the www prefix.

Solution: In your Cloudflare DNS settings, you need two separate records:

  • portfolios → A record pointing to your server IP (or CNAME to origin)

  • www.portfolios → CNAME record pointing to portfolios.shuttrbox.com

The second record is what's missing in your setup. I actually built a tool at getdnsinfo.com specifically to visualize these propagation differences. If you run a check there, you'll see exactly which global locations have picked up your www subdomain versus which are still failing—it helps isolate whether it's a DNS record issue or just propagation delay.

Q: Typescript error when using next-connect - This expression is not callable. Type 'typeof import(...)' has no call signatures A:

This may be actually caused, by the import itself. The typescript sees your import as:

import nextConnect from "next-connect"; // <--- your's

import * as nextConnect from "next-connect"; // <--- is treated like this

which is an expected behaviour for the current import, because the correct way of accessing the function which actual has call signatures is one of the following methods:

import * as NextConnect from "next-connect";
//...
NextConnect.nextConnect({...})

OR

import { nextConnect } from "next-connect";
//...
nextConnect({...})

The above is applicable if the version of next-connect is higher then 1.0.0.
